## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The macro backdrop has shifted dramatically in the three months since the US-Israel-Iran conflict began, transforming what was expected to be a year of Fed easing into one facing potential tightening. US CPI stands at 3.95% YoY as of April [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL], while PPI is running at 2.66% MoM [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PPIACO]. The University of Michigan's final May Consumer Sentiment reading collapsed to 44.8, well below the 48.2 consensus, with year-ahead inflation expectations rising to 4.8% — a deteriorating backdrop that underscores the stagflationary pressures gripping the US economy [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-05-22/spot-gold-hits-session-low-near-4500oz-after-final-consumer-sentiment-drops].

The Federal Reserve's policy trajectory has undergone a seismic shift. Kevin Warsh was sworn in as the 17th Fed Chair on Friday, and market participants are immediately testing the new regime's resolve. Fed Governor Christopher Waller — historically one of the most dovish policymakers — declared he supports removing the "easing bias" from the policy statement, effectively signalling that the next move is equally likely to be a hike as a cut [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-22/feds-waller-ready-axe-easing-bias-though-not-advocating-rate-hikes-yet]. The effective Fed Funds Rate currently sits at 3.64% [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/FEDFUNDS], but short-term interest rate markets are now fully pricing in a rate hike, with CME FedWatch previously showing a 58% probability of at least one 25bp hike by December [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-22/gold-set-weekly-loss-oil-driven-inflation-fears-boost-rate-hike-bets].

US Treasury markets are reflecting this hawkish repricing. The 10-year yield stands at 4.57% and the 2-year at 4.08% as of May 21 [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10], producing a positively sloped curve that signals markets are pricing in both near-term tightening and eventual easing. Core PCE — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — is expected to print 3.8% YoY for April when released Thursday, and analysts at Bloomberg Economics warn this will reinforce the hawkish pivot narrative [Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/more-war-driven-inflation-seen-115519421.html].

Geopolitically, the dominant driver remains the US-Iran war that entered its third month without resolution. However, weekend reports of progress on a memorandum of understanding sparked a sharp reversal in risk assets early Monday. President Trump announced Washington and Tehran have "largely negotiated" an agreement to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which carried approximately one-fifth of global oil and LNG shipments before its closure [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/most-gulf-markets-surge-us-iran-peace-deal-expectations-2026-05-24/]. Nevertheless, the US blockade "remains in full force and effect until an agreement is reached, certified, and signed," tempering optimism [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/dollar-slumps-signs-deal-reopen-hormuz-spur-risk-appetite-2026-05-25/].

With Q1 S&P 500 earnings tracking nearly 29% YoY growth driven by AI-related heavyweights, the earnings season is largely complete and macro factors are now taking the driver's seat [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-22/ubs-lifts-sp-500-annual-forecast-robust-consumer-spending-ai-demand]. UBS raised its 2026 S&P 500 year-end target to 7,900, while Morgan Stanley forecasts 8,000, both citing AI infrastructure demand and resilient consumer spending, though analysts warn that rising bond yields and post-earnings-season macro headwinds could cause a "rocky patch" for equities [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-22/wall-st-week-ahead-soaring-stocks-could-face-rocky-patch-earnings-wind].
